content.value_statement: Authoring effective Claude Code skills requires knowing structure, trigger phrasing, and progressive disclosure. This skill provides a step-by-step process and best practices to produce lean, discoverable skills that load only when needed.
actual_capabilities: Explains the required SKILL.md structure and optional scripts, references, and assets directories.
Provides a six-step process for creating a skill, from examples to iteration.
Teaches progressive disclosure so metadata, body, and resources load at the right time.
Shows how to write third-person descriptions with concrete trigger phrases.
Gives a validation checklist covering structure, description quality, and writing style.
Lists common mistakes to avoid with paired bad and good examples.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not generate or install a skill for the user.
It targets Claude Code plugin skills, not other plugin systems.
It does not execute code, run scripts, or modify files on its own.
Word-count and structure targets are recommendations, not enforced rules.

use_cases.title: Create a first plugin skill
use_cases.description: A developer new to Claude Code follows the six-step process to build a working skill with correct structure and metadata.
use_cases.target_user: Plugin developers new to skill authoring

use_cases.title: Improve a skill description
use_cases.description: A maintainer rewrites a vague description into a third-person format with specific trigger phrases so the skill loads reliably.

use_cases.title: Reorganize skill content
use_cases.description: A technical writer applies progressive disclosure to move detailed material out of SKILL.md and into reference files.

prompt_templates.title: Start a new skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a new skill for my Claude Code plugin that handles PDF rotation.

prompt_templates.title: Strengthen the description
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve the description in my SKILL.md so it triggers on the right user phrases.

prompt_templates.title: Apply progressive disclosure
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my SKILL.md and move detailed sections into reference files to keep the body lean.

prompt_templates.title: Validate before release
prompt_templates.prompt: Run through the validation checklist for my skill and list any structure, description, or writing-style issues to fix.

output_examples.input: Help me create a skill for rotating PDFs in my plugin.
output_examples.output: The skill guides you to first collect concrete usage examples, then plan a reusable rotate script and reference file, create the directory structure, write a lean SKILL.md with a third-person trigger description, and finally validate and test the result.

output_examples.input: My skill description is 'Provides hook guidance.' Is that good?
output_examples.output: That description is too vague. The skill recommends a third-person version with concrete trigger phrases, such as one that names actions like create a hook or add a PreToolUse hook so Claude Code loads the skill at the right time.

best_practices: Write descriptions in third person and include the exact phrases users would say to trigger the skill.
Keep SKILL.md lean at roughly 1,500 to 2,000 words and move detailed material into reference files.
Write the body in imperative form and reference every bundled script, example, and asset.
anti_patterns: Writing vague descriptions without concrete trigger phrases.
Placing all content in one large SKILL.md instead of using progressive disclosure.
Using second-person phrasing instead of direct imperative instructions.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It provides guidance for creating effective, well-structured skills for Claude Code plugins.

faq.question: Does it write the skill for me?
faq.answer: It guides the process and best practices. You still author and place the files in your plugin.

faq.question: What files does a skill need?
faq.answer: A skill requires a SKILL.md file with YAML frontmatter. Scripts, references, and assets are optional.

faq.question: How long should SKILL.md be?
faq.answer: Aim for roughly 1,500 to 2,000 words in the body and keep it under 5,000 words.

faq.question: What is progressive disclosure?
faq.answer: It is a loading model where metadata is always present, the body loads when the skill triggers, and resources load only when needed.

faq.question: How do I make a skill trigger reliably?
faq.answer: Write a third-person description that lists the concrete phrases users are likely to say for the task.
